source.title: Generalization in Neural Networks Through the Lens of Magnitude Potential
source.authors: Sahel Torkamani; Henry Gouk; Rik Sarkar

record.tranche_reason: Applies a new geometric measure to memorization and training dynamics, reporting results on CIFAR-100, a toy classification task, modular addition, and CIFAR-10.
record.gate_note: The paper reports correlations between magnitude-potential ratios and Feldman memorization scores, plus changes in the measure during training. It does not test the listed versions’ interventions or conditions.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a logit-space geometric measure of memorization and training dynamics, not any of V1–V8. Using published Feldman memorization scores as a reference does not test V8's removal-and-retraining effect. Its relative-flatness comparisons also do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or ranking of generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: MP ratio correlates negatively with per-example memorization scores, tracks decision-boundary changes, provides a leading indicator of grokking, and remains informative when neural collapse is suppressed. These are conclusions about the proposed geometric measure, not tests of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces and evaluates magnitude-potential ratio as a geometric measure; it does not reproduce the listed versions’ interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The scaling parameter t changes sensitivity and correlation strength; the authors report qualitatively similar trajectories across tested t values. Random subsampling also affects MP-ratio computation.

fits_no_version.finding: MP ratio correlates negatively with published Feldman memorization scores, with Spearman correlations from −0.620 to −0.763; single-checkpoint baselines are also evaluated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Logit-space MP ratio predicts per-example memorization scores in the tested CIFAR-100 ResNet-50 setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation MP-ratio dispersion changes alongside decision-boundary geometry despite nearly perfect validation accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MP-ratio dispersion detects representation changes that accuracy does not distinguish in the tested Gaussian classification task.

fits_no_version.finding: Training MP-ratio changes precede the validation-accuracy transition during modular-addition grokking.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MP-ratio trajectories provide a leading geometric indicator of grokking in the tested modular-addition setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard and Anti-NC training produce nearly identical MP-ratio trajectories on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Similar MP-ratio trajectories can occur with and without neural-collapse suppression in the tested ResNet-18 setting.

record.problems: The authors note that t was chosen mainly by trial and error, grokking experiments use small setups, and magnitude computation requires matrix inversion that can be costly on large datasets. The reported experiments cover a limited set of architectures and datasets.

untested.parts: Matched random-label and natural-label training, including random-label held-out accuracy.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under comparable tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps across comparably fitted convolutional networks, including ranking against other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples, retraining, and comparing test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, not because the reported correlations or trajectories are unreadable. Additional method evaluations, including top-500 overlap and Transformer grokking, do not supply missing tests of these versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label performance.
Test error as network width increases beyond interpolation.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness compared with training-test gaps and other measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: 2-hidden-layer MLP, widths d → 64 → 32 → K
rows.operation_detail: Tracked validation MP-ratio mean and standard deviation during training

conditions.value: three isotropic Gaussian classes in R2; 80 samples per class; 70/30 train/validation

rows.measure: Validation MP-ratio standard deviation and decision-boundary changes
rows.value: Standard deviation drops during epochs 150 to 250, then increases after epoch 250; authors describe the latter as a geometric signal of overfitting.
rows.note: The text describes the direction and timing of changes; no numeric MP-ratio values are stated.
rows.check: The trajectory description broadly matches the text, but epochs 150–250 are described as the low-dispersion stable phase. Later overfitting is the authors' geometric interpretation while validation accuracy remains near 100%; no listed version is measured.

source_check.correct: Validation MP-ratio standard deviation first drops, is low during the stable phase at epochs 150–250, and increases after epoch 250 while the mean remains high. Validation accuracy remains near 100%; the authors interpret the later dispersion increase as geometric evidence of overfitting.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5.1, paragraphs preceding Figure 3, especially lines 477–485; Figure 3 caption.
source_check.problem: Epochs 150–250 describe the low-dispersion stable phase, not the interval over which standard deviation drops.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP without bias terms, Rp → R512 → Rp
rows.operation_detail: Tracked training and validation MP-ratio mean and standard deviation through modular-addition training

conditions.value: SGD, η = 1.0, λ = 10−4, no momentum, full-batch

rows.measure: Training and validation MP-ratio trajectories in relation to accuracy transition
rows.value: Training MP-ratio rise and standard-deviation decrease precede the validation-accuracy transition; ratios and their standard deviations stabilize as validation accuracy approaches 100%.
rows.note: The paper presents these as geometric signals of generalization dynamics; exact transition values are not stated.
rows.check: The reported trajectories match the text. Grokking on fixed modular-addition labels does not test random-label capacity, width effects, or optimizer or batch-size comparisons.

relation.reason: The introduction and related work discuss memorization capacity and generalization, but the study's experiments address MP-ratio performance rather than any listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates a geometric proxy and its training trajectories without testing or operationally using a V1–V8 finding. Memorization-score correlation does not test V8's removal-and-retraining effect; relative-flatness trajectories do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation ranking.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately summarized. These rows describe the proposed measure and its comparators, rather than evidence on V1–V8; several long row fields are truncated in the supplied pack.
